The app has no `app/api/**/route.*` files and no existing server-side PostHog capture, so `posthog-node` was not needed. npm recorded the resolved browser SDK specification as `^1.442.1` in the manifest and lockfile; later client initialization can import `posthog-js`.
handoff.forNextAgent: Use `posthog-js` for client-side initialization. No server-side PostHog SDK was installed because this project currently has no API route handlers or server event-sending code.

handoff.goals: Initialize PostHog once for the Next.js App Router browser client, configure the public environment variables, and document them for developers.
handoff.did: Created `instrumentation-client.ts` as the Next.js 16 browser init point. It imports the shared default `posthog-js` client, reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST`, throws the required clear development error when either is absent, remains a production no-op when configuration is missing, and calls `posthog.init()` once when both are present. Initialization enables exception capture and development debug logging without disabling default autocapture or session recording. Updated `.env.example` with placeholder PostHog key names and configured the actual public token and host in `.env.local` through the wizard environment tool. This enables baseline pageviews, autocapture, session replay, and error capture for subsequent event instrumentation.
handoff.forNextAgent: Call sites should import the default client from `posthog-js`; `instrumentation-client.ts` initializes that singleton early and no provider was added. Use snake_case for any new event names and do not send PII in event properties. The PostHog SDK package was not present in `package.json` when inspected; the separate install task shown in the workflow queue should add `posthog-js` before review/build. No app CSP was found, so no `script-src`, `connect-src`, or `worker-src` directives were changed.
handoff.evidence: Read back `instrumentation-client.ts` and `.env.example` after writing. `check_env_keys` confirmed both `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST` are present in `.env.local`. Searched project configuration for CSP directives and found no application CSP. No builds, linters, or tests were run, per task instruction.
handoff.assumptions: Assumed the independent SDK installation task will add `posthog-js`, because it was not declared in the manifest at inspection time and this task was scoped to initialization. The app is Next.js 16.4.3, so `instrumentation-client.ts` is supported.
handoff.conflict: No conflict; the SDK dependency installation is owned by a separate workflow task.

handoff.goals: Identify users at the appropriate authentication boundary so browser events and errors share the app’s stable user identifier.
handoff.did: No files were changed. The project is a public Next.js marketing and quote-request site with browser PostHog initialization already in place, but no login, registration, session, account, or logout flow. The quote form collects contact details only to email a request; those fields are PII and are not an authenticated/stable application identity, so they must not be used for posthog.identify().
handoff.forNextAgent: There is no identity context for later client-side PostHog calls to inherit. Keep quote form names, email addresses, phone numbers, addresses, business names, and free-text details out of PostHog event properties. If authenticated accounts are added later, identify only after the client receives a guaranteed stable user primary key, attach email/name as person properties if appropriate, and reset on logout/account switch.
handoff.evidence: Searched all application, component, and library TypeScript/JavaScript files for authentication/session/login/logout/account patterns. The only user-entered flow found is app/contact/quote-form.tsx, which submits QuoteData to the server action in app/contact/actions.ts; that action uses the PII solely for Resend email delivery. package.json contains no authentication library or identity provider dependency.
handoff.assumptions: Assumed the publicly accessible quote requester is not an application account because no durable user record, session, credential, or stable user identifier exists in the project code.

handoff.goals: Make uncaught Next.js App Router errors reach PostHog through the framework-supported global error boundary, without manual captures scattered across the application.
handoff.did: Created `app/global-error.tsx`, a client-side Next.js global error boundary. It reports the framework-provided unhandled error once with `posthog.captureException(error)`, feeding PostHog Error Tracking with exception metadata. The boundary supplies the required `html` and `body` tags, renders Next.js's standard error component, and offers a retry action via `reset`.
handoff.forNextAgent: The browser SDK is initialized earlier in `instrumentation-client.ts`, including `capture_exceptions: true`. The new global boundary complements that autocapture by reporting errors Next.js catches and renders through its global error UI. No server-side exception handler was added because this task was limited to the App Router global boundary and the prior handoff establishes no server PostHog SDK.
handoff.evidence: Read `app/global-error.tsx` after creation and confirmed it is a `'use client'` global error component that calls `posthog.captureException(error)` from a `useEffect` keyed to the error. No build, lint, test, install, or app-start command was run, as instructed.
handoff.assumptions: Assumed the project uses the root `app/` App Router directory, confirmed by listing that directory; the previous initialization handoff states Next.js 16.4.3 and singleton browser SDK initialization.

handoff.goals: Select and instrument meaningful PostHog events for the Next.js marketing and quote-request site, following the prior identify handoff’s anonymous-event guidance.
handoff.did: Created `.posthog-wizard-cache/.posthog-events.json` with the five-event analytics contract. Updated `app/contact/quote-form.tsx` to import the initialized browser PostHog singleton and capture `quote_form_started` when a visitor selects a property type, `quote_form_step_completed` only after a quote step validates, and `quote_request_submitted` only after the quote server action succeeds. Submission properties are limited to the bounded property type, service count, and static service IDs; no contact or free-text form data is captured. Updated `app/components/services-explorer.tsx` to capture `service_category_selected` only when the visitor actually switches categories. Updated `app/components/services-scene.tsx` to capture `service_estimate_started` only when a visitor opens the quote form from an estimate-oriented service card, with the bounded static service ID. These events support a quote-conversion funnel and service-interest analysis.
handoff.forNextAgent: The site has no account, login, or stable customer identity, so all new browser events are intentionally personless and rely on PostHog’s anonymous browser distinct ID. Do not add quote contact fields, addresses, business names, or free-text notes to events. Review should verify the five captures and the manifest; no build, lint, or test was run by this task per instruction.
handoff.evidence: Read back each modified handler and the event manifest after editing. A capture-call search confirmed exactly the planned five custom capture locations: three in `app/contact/quote-form.tsx`, one in `app/components/services-explorer.tsx`, and one in `app/components/services-scene.tsx`.
handoff.assumptions: Assumed that the quote delivery action’s successful response is the appropriate client-side milestone for the quote submission conversion; no server-side capture was added because the prior workflow found no applicable server PostHog SDK integration and the app has no authenticated identity.
